newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO'S IXE RATCHETS UP 1997 GDP GROWTH FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO'S IXE RATCHETS UP 1997 GDP GROWTH FORECAST.

text.p: Due to unexpected strength in the Mexican economy, Mexican brokerage IXE said on Monday it has ratcheted its 1997 gross domestic product increase forecast up.
"Due to the dynamism the economy has registered, we have changed our prediction for GDP for the whole year from 4.8 percent to 5.2 percent," Grupo Financiero IXE said in a statement.
"For the second quarter of the year we estimate it will rise 5.5 percent," it added.
Second quarter GDP data is due for release on August 19.
IXE also estimated third quarter GDP growth of 5.3 percent, and 4.9 percent for the fourth.
The brokerage said the stronger economic growth has begun to translate into higher employment levels and a gradual improvement in domestic consumption.

It also pointed to July's monthly inflation figure of 0.87 percent -- the lowest so far this year -- and industrial production data for May that showed what it described as remarkably homogeneous growth among all sectors. ((--Caroline Brothers, Mexico City newsroom +525 728 7905))
